data.name: Amelon
data.detailed_description:
It's the year 2047. Bionic prostheses are extremely prevalent in the world. People blindly buy bionic organs. The fact that the protheses break down after a short time was not classified, but was mostly overlooked and neglected by the richest part of population. One of the largest factories in this industry, Pjural, stored industrial waste in a properly designated sector D. The waste was stored underground. Many talented people have been extracting, reworking and selling these parts.
The first town of Landfill was founded and Sector D began to grow. There, we meet our hero who after many years spent in the sector had ceased to resemble a human.

The main character, Amelon, leads the life of a hermit. Everything that he has achieved, he achieved by himself. His house consists of a small junkyard, a charging station, a film projector, a windmill, and a machine that extracts parts from the underground. His day consists of collecting and extracting parts. However, such a large number of bionic prostheses disturbs memory. Every day he remembers less and less. He distances himself from his past and forgets his relatives. Amelon is aware of the danger, so he records a message for himself about where and who he is. The day is coming when he doesn't remember anything.




We wake up in a place that is unknown to us and listen to the news to find out what to do. We break the monotony of our life and make contact with others. We travel the sector D, performing various missions. There are many riddles, difficult choices and adventures on the way. We can collect new items, improve mining machines and the like. In the meantime, memories of the past come back to us for unknown reasons.

  • the Game Lasts Up to Two Hours.
  • there Are Thirteen Achievements to Collect.
  • The game contains two different endings, depending on the choices throughout the game.
  • game includes English dubbing
  • a lot of puzzle
  • arcade challenges
  • humour
  • the possibility of developing your own house
  • trade system
  • side missions


  • Remember and understand your own past
  • Enter the forgotten but unique world of the Sector D. Explore the small cities and discover one-of-a-kind world.
  • Collect and extract materials from underground, and then sell what you gathered. For the earned money, buy mining machines and windmills producing necessary energy. Buy elements for your vehicle and much more.
  • Solve problems and complete missions. Take sensible decisions that greatly impact the plot.

If you want to see my next games with good graphics please support me on patreon

reviews.review:
[b]Amelon[/b] is a bizarre low-budget indie title set in a future where replacing body parts with mechanical parts is common practice. You play as Amelon, a cyborg, who aims to… well, I’m not sure what his purpose is actually. Despite the clear effort put in by the solo developer, the game is quite buggy and is not particularly fun to play.
 
[h1][u]Positive:[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*]Impressive amount of features for a solo-developer. While there are a lot of flaws in the game, I can appreciate the effort Pjural made to introduce variety. The helicopter segment, for example, was quite good (although it was very difficult to control).
[/list]

[h1][u]Neutral:[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*]It is clear that the voice actors are not native English speakers. However, considering the low-budget, I can live with this. What bothered me more was that the subtitles don’t always match the what is being said. I imagine this isn’t difficult to fix.
[*]I would like to see some improvement in the main menu. For example, when selecting the language for the subtitle (Polish or English), it would be nice if there was some sort of indicator to which one was chosen. As it currently is, you just have to click on the language and hope that it worked. I’d also like to see the addition of display and audio options in-game. 
[*]The addition of shortcuts, like pressing “i” to open the item menu, and key remapping would be nice as well.
[*]I found movement awkward. As it currently is, the horizontal directional keys cause Amelon to rotate clock- or anti-clockwise. This, combined with the fixed camera (which can be manually rotated) often caused me to bump into objects and struggle with precise movement. I would have preferred it if the direction Amelon is facing is determined by the mouse pointer and the horizontal directional keys would cause him to strafe instead of rotate. I find that this would improve movement fluidity tremendously. 
[*]I managed to get out of bounds. See screenshots here: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1368147029]Out of bounds 1,[/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1368147200]out of bounds 2.[/url]
[/list]

[h1][u]Negative:[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*]Very bizarre choice in music. “Oh you touch my tralala” song, nyan cat theme, “sittin’ on the toilet” lady, and the song Brook plays in One Piece are just some of the pieces I came across. It’s a very random collection of pop culture references that honestly seem out of place. I’m not sure how I should react to this. 
[*]I found the hospital segment very confusing, it took me a while before I realized what had to be done. I don’t think the game should expect the player to press the help/guidance to progress - the instructions should be given in a more natural way.
[*]I’m pretty sure the save/load function is bugged. If I save, perform an action with an NPC, and then load, the action will be carried through. To counter this, I have to save, exit the game, and then load. Furthermore, when I returned to the game (after not playing for some time) I found more bugs. For example, when I enter a certain area, I get a pop-up saying I don’t have the map for that area (even though I do and can clearly see it on the map), and I had to redo some quests.
[*]I found that the game was very monotone - the colour palate was basically different shades of brown and grey. While this is probably intentional, to set the tone of the game, it gets very tiresome to look at it for long periods of time. It doesn’t help that most of the map is essentially empty desert. 
[*]I reached a point in the game where there was no clear objective. Since there is no quest log (or something similar) I was unsure of how to progress. Basically I drove around talking to NPCs to see what could be done. After 30 minutes of aimless driving I decided to stop. It simply wasn’t worth my time. 
[/list]
 
[h1][u]Conclusion:[/u][/h1]
[h1]★✬☆☆☆ Needs more work[/h1]
I’m a big supporter of solo/low-budget developers. Game development is not an easy process, especially if you’re doing most of it alone. Having said that, I appreciate the time and effort into making Amelon. It is quite clear that Pjural was experimenting with many game elements and techniques. Good job in that regard. However, at the same time, Amelon feels very unfinished - it felt more like a developer’s experimental bucket of ideas rather than a complete game. I usually try to finish the game before reviewing it, but because of the bugs, lack of a clear objective, and aimless wandering, I lost interest. Amelon was not worth the time I invested in it.

[table]
[tr]
[th][h1]If you enjoyed this review please follow me on my [url=http://store.steampowered.com/curator/26827738-%27b-Reviews/?appid=241930]curator page[/url] and [url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/breviews]group[/url]. Your time and support is greatly appreciated![/h1][/th]
[/tr]
[/table]
